key_insight: KaCGM replaces opaque neural structural equations with Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) so each causal mechanism is decomposed into inspectable univariate components, yielding expressive yet auditable causal generative models for mixed-type tabular data.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between expressivity and auditability in deep causal generative models: existing black‑box architectures are powerful but hard to inspect, limiting their use in high‑stakes domains and for counterfactual reasoning on mixed‑type tabular data.
method: Parameterize each structural equation in a structural causal model with a Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) that decomposes multivariate mappings into sums/compositions of univariate functions.
Train the KaCGM on mixed‑type tabular data to answer observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries while preserving model flexibility.
Expose and inspect the KAN component functions and their contributions for each variable to enable auditability and transparent causal explanations.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, auditable causal generative model that balances interpretability and expressiveness—useful for trustworthy decision‑making, regulation, and debugging in high‑stakes applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: causal graph (SEM) where each node is a KAN block showing inner/outer univariate components.
Component decomposition plot: example univariate component functions and their weighted sum producing a variable.
Counterfactual flowchart: sequence showing observational data → intervention on a variable → generated counterfactual outcome.
Trade‑off chart: performance (fidelity/ATE accuracy) vs interpretability comparing KaCGM and black‑box baselines.
paper_authors: Alejandro Almodóvar, Mar Elizo, Patricia A. Apellániz, Santiago Zazo, Juan Parras
